Call the leg adjacent to \theta x, the leg opposite it y, and the hypotenuse r. Arctangent returns opposite over adjacent, so take y=4 and x=3; then r=\sqrt{x^2+y^2}=\sqrt{9+16}=\sqrt{25}=5.

By the right-triangle definitions, \sin\theta=\frac{y}{r}, \cos\theta=\frac{x}{r}, \tan\theta=\frac{y}{x}, \csc\theta=\frac{r}{y}, \sec\theta=\frac{r}{x}, and \cot\theta=\frac{x}{y}. This expression asks for the sine of \theta, so the definition to use is \sin\theta=\frac{y}{r}.

With x=3, y=4, and r=5, \sin\theta=\frac{y}{r}=\frac{4}{5}.

Therefore \sin\left(\arctan\left(\frac{4}{3}\right)\right)=\boxed{\frac{4}{5}}.
